key_insight: Medical world models aim to move AI in healthcare from static prediction to simulators that can represent patient states, model how disease unfolds, and compare the likely impact of different interventions.
clinical_relevance: This framework could help clinicians anticipate deterioration and explore treatment-conditioned future trajectories to support more individualized care decisions.
method: Organizes the field into three linked capabilities: patient-state construction, clinical dynamics modelling, and intervention decision support.
Synthesizes representative work across foundation models, longitudinal modelling, disease simulation, treatment-effect estimation, reinforcement learning, and digital twins.
Frames the field as a perception--dynamics--planning pipeline for healthcare.
evidence_signal: This is a review paper, so the evidence comes from comparing and integrating representative prior systems rather than reporting a new dataset or benchmark in the abstract.
watch_item: Plausible simulated rollouts may still be clinically misleading if the underlying state models, treatment effects, or evaluation settings do not generalize to real patients.
paper_title: Medical world models: representing medical states, modelling clinical dynamics and guiding intervention policies
